chunks: Our father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with them) narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris both narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Umar, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked: 'Who is the one upon whom I am compelled and whose maintenance becomes obligatory upon me?' He replied: 'The two parents, the child, and the wife.'

key_terms.نَفَقَتُهُ: maintenance or financial support provided to dependents

ai.seo_question: Who are the three relatives for whom a man must provide financial maintenance according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the primary dependents for whom a man bears the financial burden of *nafaqah*, specifically listing parents, children, and wife. This hadith serves as a foundational text in Shia fiqh for determining the hierarchy of maintenance obligations, distinguishing between obligatory support for direct lineage and spouses versus voluntary or conditional support for other relatives. It underscores the communal and familial responsibility central to Shia social ethics.
